clue.text: Take infant regularly into school

indicators.note: the regular letters are put into the abbreviation for school, which wraps round them
regularly means every other letter of the word infant is taken

explanation.surface: Someone collects a baby and takes it off to school on a regular basis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' picks the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters of 'infant', NAT, which go 'into' SCH.
explanation.definitionFit: To grab or seize something quickly is a common synonym of take.

clue.text: Executive about to empty some luggage

parts.note: a suit is slang for a business executive, from the clothes worn
CA, short for circa, means about

indicators.note: emptying a word removes its inside, leaving only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A businessman is about to clear out some of his bags.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to empty' leaves SE from 'some'; the surface invites 'some luggage' as a phrase, but 'some' is only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A case for carrying clothes when travelling is an item of baggage.

clue.text: Servant initially out to help

indicators.note: the initial letter of the servant word is put out, i.e. dropped

parts.note: a maid is a female domestic servant

explanation.surface: A servant has gone out at first to lend a hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Assistance or support offered to someone is a straightforward synonym of help.

clue.text: Officer has rifle for soldier

parts.note: CO is short for commanding officer
the contraction 's stands for has, as in 'he's got'
to rifle a place is to plunder it, which is to sack it

explanation.surface: An officer is carrying a gun meant for one of the soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rifle' looks like a gun but is the verb meaning to ransack.
explanation.definitionFit: Cossacks were Russian cavalry fighters, so one of them is a soldier.

clue.text: Listened to a season's hits

indicators.note: what is listened to is heard, so the letters are a word that sounds like the phrase

parts.note: to season food is to salt it, so a season's becomes a salt's

explanation.surface: Someone tuned in to the year's chart-topping records.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hits' looks like pop records but means blows or attacks.
explanation.definitionFit: Attacks or blows struck on someone are hits, as both nouns.

clue.text: Store trendy girl left shortly after ordering Christmas present

parts.note: to stock goods is to store them
in means fashionable or trendy

indicators.note: once put in order the letters of the girl and the shortened left are rearranged
shortly means the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: taken as written before its last letter goes

explanation.surface: A trendy shop girl leaves soon after putting in an order for a Christmas gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' cuts the last letter off 'left'; 'after ordering' then rearranges the girl with that shortened word, so 'ordering' is not about placing an order.
explanation.definitionFit: A small gift put into a hung-up stocking on Christmas Eve is a seasonal present.

clue.text: Severe wind from south and east

parts.note: Auster is the Latin name for the south wind
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A harsh wind is blowing in from the south and east.
explanation.definitionFit: Stern, strict and plain in manner are all meanings shared by these two words.

clue.text: In stick-up at a bank, perhaps, start to take money

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: to gel is to stick or set firm

indicators.note: the opening letter is placed in the middle of the assembled stick-up, a and bank pieces

parts.note: a bank is one example of a lender

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Robbers at a bank start grabbing the cash during the hold-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stick-up' is not a robbery: in a down clue 'up' reverses the word for stick. 'In' places the first letter of 'take' within everything else; 'at' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Coins and notes that must by law be accepted in payment are currency, i.e. money.

clue.text: Phone card I provided for girl

parts.note: a SIM card is the chip that makes a mobile phone work
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: Someone supplies a phone card for a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Simone is a female first name, and crosswords often define names as girl.

clue.text: Maybe begged for a Sunday morning treat?

definitions.text: Maybe begged for a Sunday morning treat?

parts.words: Maybe begged for a Sunday morning treat
parts.note: the word begged split as B-EGG-ED shows an egg, a morning meal, lying inside a bed

explanation.walkthrough: 'begged' looks like pleaded, but split up it is EGG (a morning meal) in B-ED, the picture of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A morning meal served to someone still lying down is a lazy weekend indulgence.

clue.text: Toiling hard in Brazilian location, American breathes in powdery stuff

indicators.note: breathing in takes the powder into the body of the other pieces

parts.note: taken as written
Rio de Janeiro is a city in Brazil
US is short for the United States, so American
dust is fine powdery matter

explanation.surface: A hard-working American in Rio inhales some dusty powder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breathes in' acts on the whole string of in, Rio and American, the powder landing straight after the first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone diligent and hard-working is labouring busily, an adjective matching the phrase.

clue.text: Podgy men might shed a lot here

definitions.text: Podgy men might shed a lot here

indicators.note: losing most of their letters, the two words keep only a short run from their middle

explanation.surface: Overweight men can lose plenty of weight at this place.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines; 'might shed a lot' also tells you to drop most letters of 'Podgy men'.
explanation.definitionFit: A fitness centre is where people work out and lose weight.

clue.text: Ice cream son had in Luigi's house with thanks

indicators.note: a house that has someone in contains them, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: casa is Italian for house, and Luigi is a typical Italian name
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
ta is British informal for thank you

explanation.surface: A son ate ice cream at Luigi's home and said thank you.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassata is an Italian ice-cream dessert layered with fruit, so a kind of iced sweet.

clue.text: Musical technique: is it extremely underused with Elgar composition?

indicators.note: a composition is an arrangement, so the letters are put together anew

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: extremely means the extreme letters, the first and last of the word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Asks whether some guitar style is barely used in a piece by the composer Elgar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' gives UD from 'underused'; 'composition' rearranges ISIT, UD and ELGAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Playing a guitar by sliding a bar or bottleneck along the strings is a style of playing.

clue.text: Thousands queue endlessly to welcome queen back in centre of government

indicators.note: welcoming someone takes them in, so the turned queen goes inside

parts.note: K and M are both abbreviations for thousand, so the plural gives both

indicators.note: back means the word is read the other way round

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

indicators.note: endlessly means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: a line is a queue

explanation.surface: Thousands queue to greet a returning queen at the seat of power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thousands' is plural, so both thousand abbreviations are used; 'back' reverses the queen, which sits between them.
explanation.definitionFit: The Moscow citadel houses the Russian government and stands for its seat of power.

clue.text: Like a thief, without clean hands?

definitions.meaning: literally having hands covered in something gluey

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is literal: hands that are not clean may be gummy.
explanation.definitionFit: Light-fingered thieves let things stick to their hands, and messy hands are gluey.

clue.text: I'm busy going round about, as requested

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

indicators.note: going round means the police word encircles the short word for about

parts.note: busy is British slang for a police officer, as is plod
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone says they are busy doing the rounds, as they were asked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'busy' is slang for a policeman, and PLOD (from Mr Plod in children's books) is another.
explanation.definitionFit: Begged earnestly is a stronger way of saying asked for something.

clue.text: As something worth listening to, poem's words fail miserably

indicators.note: failing miserably suggests a wreck, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the apostrophe is ignored, giving fourteen letters

explanation.surface: A poem's words fall flat, so is it really worth hearing?
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is plural in sense: wise sayings collectively are worth hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Wise sayings or sage advice are things a listener ought to heed.

clue.text: Form of transport making you rant and complain endlessly

parts.note: to rail is to rant or protest angrily

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter is removed

parts.note: to carp is to complain

explanation.surface: Some kind of travel makes you rant and moan without end.
explanation.definitionFit: A single self-powered carriage running on tracks is a means of getting about.

clue.text: Trio's pieces will include new Italian church music

indicators.note: including something holds it inside, so the new letter goes in
broken into pieces, the letters of the trio are scattered and rearranged

parts.note: the possessive is no letter, giving the four letters of trio
IT is short for Italian, as in Italian vermouth

explanation.surface: A trio's musical pieces will feature a new Italian church anthem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pieces' signals rearranging the trio, not musical works; 'will include' then puts the letter for new inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A psalm or antiphon sung as the priest approaches the altar opens the Mass.

clue.text: Dog kept being nibbled by pig

indicators.note: something nibbled is held in the mouth, so the word sits inside the pig word

parts.note: a sow is a female pig
had means kept or held

explanation.surface: A dog that was kept is having bits bitten by a pig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog' looks like the animal but is the verb to follow closely.
explanation.definitionFit: To follow someone closely and secretly is to tail them, a verb sense matching dog.

clue.text: Entertainer bound to make big noise, I found, after 45 minutes

indicators.note: after means the noise and I follow the time piece

parts.note: three quarters of an hour is the first three of its four letters
a din is a loud noise

explanation.surface: A performer, tied up, is sure to make a racket after three quarters of an hour.
explanation.walkthrough: '45 minutes' is three quarters of HOUR, its first three letters; 'bound' hints at the escapologist.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous escapologist performed on stage, so he was a showman.

clue.text: Shoot after being confronted by gangster

parts.note: later means afterwards
Al Capone is the archetypal gangster

explanation.surface: A man is shot dead after a gangster confronts him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoot' is botanical: a side branch from a stem.
explanation.definitionFit: A side shoot growing out from a main stem is called by this adjective used as a noun.

clue.text: Serve time? One's coming to end of sentence

definitions.text: One's coming to end of sentence

parts.note: to do time is to serve a prison sentence, so serve gives do

explanation.surface: A prisoner asks whether to serve time as his sentence nears its end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sentence' looks like a prison term but is a grammatical sentence ending in a full stop.
explanation.definitionFit: A full stop is a small point marking where a written sentence finishes.

clue.text: Journalist prompt to imbibe British beer

indicators.note: imbibing takes something in, so the British letters go inside

parts.note: a cue is a prompt given to an actor
porter is a dark beer

explanation.surface: A reporter is urged to down a British beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A young, inexperienced newspaper writer is a junior member of the press.

clue.text: Pull away from east, presumably

parts.note: heading away from east suggests going to the west
W is the compass abbreviation for west

explanation.surface: Someone pulls a load away from the east, as one would suppose.
explanation.walkthrough: Moving away from the east is presumably heading towards the west, which the parse splits into two short pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To haul a vehicle behind with a rope is to drag it along.

clue.text: Winning her, one had "trouble and strife"?

definitions.text: Winning her, one had "trouble and strife"?

parts.words: Winning her, one had "trouble and strife"
parts.note: trouble and strife is Cockney rhyming slang for wife, and here also the conflict in which she was won

explanation.walkthrough: In Cockney rhyming slang 'trouble and strife' means wife; here the trouble and strife is also a war.

clue.text: Carrying weight, horse was in agitated state

parts.note: a steed is a horse

explanation.surface: A horse carrying weight got itself worked up.
